# GripConstraint

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/GripConstraint.cs#L23)

Limits how the object may move while it is held by the grip point this sits on.

A door hinges, a drawer slides, a valve turns, a power cell twists and then pulls out. In
every one of them the *object* is what moves and the hand goes with it, which is why
this clamps the pose the hold wants for the body rather than sliding the grip point along it.

On the grip point rather than on the grabbable, because which way a thing may move depends on
where it is held. The same cabinet taken by its drawer front and by its door handle moves two
different ways, and each grip point says which.

Several on one point are normal and compose: turn about an axis and then slide along it is two
of these, and a [`GripSequence`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/GripSequence) decides which is free at any moment. Anything no
constraint allows is held still - a mechanism is what the object may do, so everything else is
what it may not.

```csharp
public abstract class GripConstraint : MonoBehaviour
```

### Reference {#reference}

Where the hand was asking the object to be at the moment this constraint last became free to
move, and how far along its travel the object was then.

Everything this allows is measured from here, so what drives a mechanism is how far the hand
has travelled since it took hold - never the gap between hand and object. A hand closes a
few centimetres off the grip, and on a mechanism that gap is a lever arm that would read
as travel nobody asked for. A sequenced mechanism shows it worst: a stage that watched the
hand while it was held shut would cash the whole accumulated wander in on the step it
opened.

```csharp
public Pose Reference { get; }
```

**Returns** [`Pose`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Pose.html)

### EnsureRest() {#ensurerest}

Remembers where the object rests.

Once, and never again: rest is the closed door, the shut drawer, the seated cell, and it
has to survive the thing being opened and let go of. Read lazily rather than in Awake so a
mechanism can be driven in the editor too.
